failures.failure: A persisted ALLOW policy with empty scope is admitted by load(); downstream authorization can therefore treat the capability as unrestricted.
failures.architectural_law: Persisted authority must be revalidated at every trust-boundary load; an invalid grant may never become broader authority by omission.

failures.source: State Register distributed authority tests and protocol
failures.failure: Compaction/recovery can destroy the original quorum evidence needed to prove idempotent authority-event retry unless snapshots retain the committed entry and certificate.
failures.architectural_law: Compaction may not erase proof needed to distinguish exact retry from conflicting replay.

failures.failure: A stale recovery path can resurrect consumed authority unless consumed nonces/tombstones are part of certified recoverable state.
failures.architectural_law: Consumed authority is monotonic across restart, snapshot, compaction, partition and recovery.

failures.failure: Predicate truth can be claimed independently of the evidence record that allegedly establishes it.
failures.architectural_law: Every predicate evaluation must bind to exact admitted evidence identities and values.

failures.failure: Conflict handling can mask a direct failed or unknown predicate if conflict resolution is evaluated first.
failures.architectural_law: Direct violated preconditions and load-bearing unknowns dominate conflict resolution; conflict search cannot erase failure.

failures.failure: A runtime accepted a caller-supplied authority capability dictionary, allowing the caller to manufacture the VM authority context.
failures.architectural_law: Positive authority context must come only from a trusted signed assertion bound to the exact state/operation and from the Authority Ledger's own permit snapshot.

failures.failure: An adapter could be invoked directly with a consequence object without proof that the Effect Gateway mediated the call.
failures.architectural_law: Every adapter call requires a gateway-signed invocation bound to permit, prepared intent, consequence, adapter identity and gateway key.

failures.failure: Execution receipt hashes and observer names provided integrity labels but not cryptographic identity, permitting forged executor/observer claims.
failures.architectural_law: Execution receipts and independent observations require trusted signatures; unknown keys and executor-as-observer substitution fail closed.

failures.failure: An effect transition could be committed while its permit remained ISSUED, allowing multiple pending effect transitions to reference the same authority before gateway consumption.
failures.architectural_law: Effect-transition commit must durably PREPARE the exact permit intent before canonical commit; restart resumes only that prepared intent.

failures.failure: Evidence and identity registries initially existed only in memory, so transition history could survive restart while the proof material supporting admission and identity verification disappeared.
failures.architectural_law: Proof registries are append-only durable stores whose hashes/signatures must replay and verify across restart; missing proof material fails closed.
